methods.label: Find an identity shared by the two bases
methods.explanation:
Take \(n\) to be an integer, as in the recorded sequence interpretation. The second base is negative, so an unrestricted real-index interpretation would require further domain information.

Each term of \(f(n)\) is a constant times a power. To compare shifted indices, look for an identity involving the square of each base. Write
\[
r=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad
s=\frac{1-\sqrt5}{2},
\]
and let \(A=\frac{5+3\sqrt5}{10}\), \(B=\frac{5-3\sqrt5}{10}\). Then \(f(n)=Ar^n+Bs^n\).

For either choice \(t=r\) or \(t=s\), direct expansion gives
\[
t^2=\frac{6\pm2\sqrt5}{4}
=\frac{3\pm\sqrt5}{2}
=t+1.
\]
Both bases are nonzero, so integer power laws apply even when a shifted exponent is zero or negative. Factoring the lower power now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
t^{n+1}-t^{n-1}
&=t^{n-1}(t^2-1)\\
&=t^{n-1}t=t^n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying this identity separately to the two terms yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n+1)-f(n-1)
&=A(r^{n+1}-r^{n-1})\\
&\quad+B(s^{n+1}-s^{n-1})\\
&=Ar^n+Bs^n=f(n).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, for the recorded integer indices, the answer is \(f(n)\), choice B.
